title_candidates: DeepMind's agent-control roadmap says trust needs brakes
summary: Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap treats powerful internal agents like systems that need permissions, monitoring, and fast intervention.

primary_source.title: Securing the future of AI agents
primary_source.author: Google DeepMind
key_facts: Google DeepMind published a safety post about securing internal systems against increasingly capable AI agents.
The post describes an AI Control Roadmap that adds system-level security on top of model alignment.
DeepMind frames advanced internal agents as potential insider threats for threat-modeling purposes.
The roadmap emphasizes detection, prevention, response, and metrics such as coverage, recall, and time-to-response.

prerequisites: Any AI agent or automation that can read files, call tools, edit data, or run code

steps.instruction: List the tools your agent can use today, including file access, network access, code execution, and write permissions.
Mark each tool as low-risk, reversible, sensitive, or high-risk.
Require approval for sensitive and high-risk actions before the agent can execute them.
Log every tool call, then review one real run for unexpected reads, writes, or external calls.
Write down who can stop the agent and how quickly they can do it.
